Hi all — taking a first stab at the plain-language copy you requested. I kept it short and non-technical for procurement teams. Happy to tweak.

PUBLIC-FACING BLURB (1–2 lines)
"Redwood processes customer inputs in the region(s) you select when you create a deployment. For our hosted API, customer data is typically processed in EU or US cloud regions; we do not use customer content for model training. Where necessary, we rely on subprocessors (cloud providers and monitoring services) — we publish an up-to-date list and notify customers 30 days before adding any new subprocessor."

FAQ ENTRY (expanded, 3 short bullets)
- Where is my data processed?
  We process requests in the region you choose (EU or US). Some operational metadata (logs, metrics) may be replicated to our central control plane for billing and troubleshooting; sensitive content is not used to train models.
- Are subprocessors used?
  Yes — our subprocessors include cloud hosting, monitoring, and logging vendors. We maintain a public matrix and a subscription-based notification list.
- How will I be notified if a new subprocessor is added?
  Customers who opt into notifications receive an email 30 days before onboarding; we also publish updates on the privacy page and in the Console admin changelog.

Notes: I left the 30-day notice consistent with our DPA redline. Kimberly, flag anything that needs revision for procurement audiences. Elena — if you want the 1-line version even shorter I can tighten to a single sentence.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this is good for procurement. Two small legal clarifications I recommend we surface to FinServ’s vendor team (can be parenthetical or in the FAQ):

1) Cross-border transfers: We typically rely on standard contractual protections and appropriate legal mechanisms where data is routed between regions. For customers with specific adequacy requirements, we can add contractual commitments in the DPA.
2) Notification mechanism: We should offer the option for FinServ to receive change notices via a signed security portal webhook in addition to email (helps larger vendors automate ingestion).

Elena — if FinServ requires a particular transfer mechanism (e.g., SCCs or a DPA clause), let us know and we’ll surface it in the DPA redline. Otherwise, we’re comfortable confirming the 30-day notification and providing the CSV as authoritative.

Kimberly
